version.changelog: Synced SKILL.md and README.md with v1.2.4 content, updated sanitization types to 26 CN plus 26 EN

llm.summary: SafeShrink appears to be a real document-optimization skill, but it asks agents to intercept broad file workflows and auto-download a proprietary Windows executable without enough scoping or verification.

dimensions.detail: The compression, sanitization, OCR, and SSD conversion capabilities match the stated purpose and are disclosed, including handling sensitive documents locally.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill declares a 'Golden Rule' that takes priority over other skills, tells the agent to stop current processing, and discourages reading original files before SafeShrink interception, even though users may have asked for ordinary file handling.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: First use instructs the AI to auto-download and cache an EXE from GitHub, with no hash, signature, or separate install consent described; the artifacts also mix 'fully offline/no internet' claims with required download and optional VirusTotal upload guidance.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The tool is meant for potentially sensitive documents, but broad triggers such as common extensions and generic file-processing phrases could invoke it in unrelated workflows.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Local caching of the EXE is disclosed and there is no clear background service or driver behavior, but caching a remotely fetched binary expands the trust boundary beyond a simple skill prompt.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a proprietary Windows document tool being downloaded from GitHub and cached locally. Confirm the exact binary source yourself, avoid automatic processing of sensitive folders, review sanitized/OCR outputs before sharing them, and do not treat antivirus allowlisting or VirusTotal upload advice as proof of safety.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: local document processing is purpose-aligned, but the artifacts overstate 'fully offline/no internet' while also requiring GitHub download and suggesting VirusTotal verification.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: automatic remote EXE download and caching is a material supply-chain concern because no integrity verification or separate user approval is specified.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded: OCR and sanitization necessarily process sensitive content for this purpose, but users should still review outputs because sanitization may be incomplete.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: activation terms include broad file extensions and common phrases, which is overbroad given the interception flow and binary execution path.
[SSD-1] unexpected: Accepted: claiming priority over other skills and blocking direct reads is not necessary for document optimization and materially affects user-directed agent behavior.
[SSD-4] unexpected: Accepted: stopping current processing before intent is established can funnel unrelated file tasks into SafeShrink, although the skill does include a later user-confirmation step.
